sanskrit: ekādaśacamūbhartā putro duryodhanas tava gadām ādāya tejasvī padātiḥ prasthito hradam
english: Your son Duryodhana, lord of eleven armies, blazing with energy, took up his mace and set out on foot toward the lake.

sanskrit: nātidūraṃ tato gatvā padbhyām eva narādhipaḥ sasmāra vacanaṃ kṣattur dharmaśīlasya dhīmataḥ
english: When the king had gone but a little way on foot, he remembered the words of Vidura, that wise man of righteous conduct.

sanskrit: idaṃ nūnaṃ mahāprājño viduro dṛṣṭavān purā mahad vaiśasam asmākaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca saṃyuge
english: "Surely the deeply wise Vidura foresaw this long ago—this great slaughter of ours and of the kṣatriyas in battle."

sanskrit: evaṃ vicintayānas tu pravivikṣur hradaṃ nṛpaḥ duḥkhasaṃtaptahṛdayo dṛṣṭvā rājan balakṣayam
english: Brooding thus, his heart scorched with grief at the sight of his army's destruction, O king, the lord wished to enter the lake.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ abhyadhāvanta saṃkruddhās tava rājan balaṃ prati
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, great king, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, enraged, rushed against your forces, O king.

sanskrit: śaktyṛṣṭiprāsahastānāṃ balānām abhigarjatām saṃkalpam akaron moghaṃ gāṇḍīvena dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: As the host roared, brandishing spears, swords, and lances in their hands, Dhanaṃjaya with his Gāṇḍīva brought their resolve to nothing.

sanskrit: tān hatvā niśitair bāṇaiḥ sāmātyān saha bandhubhiḥ rathe śvetahaye tiṣṭhann arjuno bahv aśobhata
english: Slaying them with his keen shafts, together with their counselors and kinsmen, Arjuna, standing in his chariot drawn by white horses, shone in great splendor.

sanskrit: subalasya hate putre savājirathakuñjare mahāvanam iva chinnam abhavat tāvakaṃ balam
english: When Subala's son fell with his horses, chariots, and elephants, your army became like a vast forest hewn down.

sanskrit: anekaśatasāhasre bale duryodhanasya ha nānyo mahāratho rājañ jīvamāno vyadṛśyata
english: In the host of Duryodhana, many hundreds of thousands strong, no other great warrior, O king, was seen to be left alive—

sanskrit: droṇaputrād ṛte vīrāt tathaiva kṛtavarmaṇaḥ kṛpāc ca gautamād rājan pārthivāc ca tavātmajāt
english: save the heroic son of Droṇa, and likewise Kṛtavarman, and Kṛpa of Gautama's line, O king, and your son the prince.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā hasan sātyakim abravīt kim anena gṛhītena nānenārtho 'sti jīvatā
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, seeing me, laughed and said to Sātyaki: "Why take this man captive? There is no use in his living."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnavacaḥ śrutvā śiner naptā mahārathaḥ udyamya niśitaṃ khaḍgaṃ hantuṃ mām udyatas tadā
english: Hearing Dhṛṣṭadyumna's words, Śini's grandson, that mighty warrior, raised his sharp sword and made ready to slay me then.

sanskrit: tam āgamya mahāprājñaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt mucyatāṃ saṃjayo jīvan na hantavyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: But the deeply wise Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana came up and said: "Let Saṃjaya be released alive; he must by no means be slain."

sanskrit: dvaipāyanavacaḥ śrutvā śiner naptā kṛtāñjaliḥ tato mām abravīn muktvā svasti saṃjaya sādhaya
english: Hearing Dvaipāyana's words, Śini's grandson joined his palms, then released me and said: "Fare well, Saṃjaya; go your way."

sanskrit: anujñātas tv ahaṃ tena nyastavarmā nirāyudhaḥ prātiṣṭhaṃ yena nagaraṃ sāyāhne rudhirokṣitaḥ
english: Dismissed by him, I laid aside my armor and weapons and set out toward the city at evening, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: krośamātram apakrāntaṃ gadāpāṇim avasthitam ekaṃ duryodhanaṃ rājann apaśyaṃ bhṛśavikṣatam
english: Having withdrawn about a krośa, I saw, O king, Duryodhana standing alone, mace in hand, grievously wounded.

sanskrit: sa tu mām aśrupūrṇākṣo nāśaknod abhivīkṣitum upapraikṣata māṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā dīnam avasthitam
english: His eyes brimming with tears, he could not gaze upon me; yet, seeing me standing there wretched, he looked toward me.

sanskrit: taṃ cāham api śocantaṃ dṛṣṭvaikākinam āhave muhūrtaṃ nāśakaṃ vaktuṃ kiṃ cid duḥkhapariplutaḥ
english: And I too, seeing him grieving and alone upon the field, was so overwhelmed with sorrow that for a moment I could say nothing.

sanskrit: tato 'smai tad ahaṃ sarvam uktavān grahaṇaṃ tadā dvaipāyanaprasādāc ca jīvato mokṣam āhave
english: Then I told him all of it—how I had been taken captive, and how by the grace of Dvaipāyana I had been released alive from the battle.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva ca dhyātvā pratilabhya ca cetanām bhrātṝṃś ca sarvasainyāni paryapṛcchata māṃ tataḥ
english: After brooding for a moment and recovering his senses, he then asked me about his brothers and all his armies.

sanskrit: tasmai tad aham ācakṣaṃ sarvaṃ pratyakṣadarśivān bhrātṝṃś ca nihatān sarvān sainyaṃ ca vinipātitam
english: To him I, who had seen it with my own eyes, told everything: that all his brothers were slain and his army cut down.

sanskrit: trayaḥ kila rathāḥ śiṣṭās tāvakānāṃ narādhipa iti prasthānakāle māṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: "Three warriors of your host are left, it is said, O lord of men"—so Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana had told me at the time of my departure.

sanskrit: sa dīrgham iva niḥśvasya viprekṣya ca punaḥ punaḥ aṃse māṃ pāṇinā spṛṣṭvā putras te paryabhāṣata
english: Sighing as if from the depths, and gazing about him again and again, your son touched me on the shoulder with his hand and spoke.

sanskrit: tvad anyo neha saṃgrāme kaś cij jīvati saṃjaya dvitīyaṃ neha paśyāmi sasahāyāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Save you, Saṃjaya, no one else here lives through this battle; I see no second man—while the Pāṇḍavas have their allies still."

sanskrit: brūyāḥ saṃjaya rājānaṃ prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram duryodhanas tava sutaḥ praviṣṭo hradam ity uta
english: "Tell the king, Saṃjaya—the lord whose eye is wisdom—that your son Duryodhana has entered the lake."

sanskrit: suhṛdbhis tādṛśair hīnaḥ putrair bhrātṛbhir eva ca pāṇḍavaiś ca hṛte rājye ko nu jīvati mādṛśaḥ
english: "Bereft of such friends, of sons and of brothers, and with the kingdom seized by the Pāṇḍavas, what man like me would go on living?"

sanskrit: ācakṣethāḥ sarvam idaṃ māṃ ca muktaṃ mahāhavāt asmiṃs toyahrade suptaṃ jīvantaṃ bhṛśavikṣatam
english: "Tell him all of this—and that I, escaped from the great battle, lie sleeping alive in this lake of water, sorely wounded."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja prāviśat taṃ hradaṃ nṛpaḥ astambhayata toyaṃ ca māyayā manujādhipaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, great king, the lord entered that lake, and by his magic power the king of men froze its waters firm.

sanskrit: tasmin hradaṃ praviṣṭe tu trīn rathāñ śrāntavāhanān apaśyaṃ sahitān ekas taṃ deśaṃ samupeyuṣaḥ
english: When he had entered the lake, I, alone, saw three warriors with their teams worn out coming together to that place—

sanskrit: kṛpaṃ śāradvataṃ vīraṃ drauṇiṃ ca rathināṃ varam bhojaṃ ca kṛtavarmāṇaṃ sahitāñ śaravikṣatān
english: Kṛpa, the hero of Śaradvat's line, and Droṇa's son, best of warriors, and Kṛtavarman of the Bhojas, together, all torn by arrows.

sanskrit: te sarve mām abhiprekṣya tūrṇam aśvān acodayan upayāya ca mām ūcur diṣṭyā jīvasi saṃjaya
english: All of them, catching sight of me, swiftly urged on their horses, and drawing near they said: "By good fortune you live, Saṃjaya!"

sanskrit: apṛcchaṃś caiva māṃ sarve putraṃ tava janādhipam kaccid duryodhano rājā sa no jīvati saṃjaya
english: And they all asked me about your son, the lord of men: "Does our king Duryodhana yet live, Saṃjaya?"

sanskrit: ākhyātavān ahaṃ tebhyas tadā kuśalinaṃ nṛpam tac caiva sarvam ācakṣaṃ yan māṃ duryodhano 'bravīt hradaṃ caivāham ācaṣṭa yaṃ praviṣṭo narādhipaḥ
english: I told them then that the king was unharmed, and I recounted all that Duryodhana had said to me, and I pointed out the lake into which the king of men had entered.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu tad rājan niśamya vacanaṃ mama taṃ hradaṃ vipulaṃ prekṣya karuṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: But Aśvatthāman, O king, hearing my words and gazing upon that broad lake, lamented piteously.

sanskrit: aho dhiṅ na sa jānāti jīvato 'smān narādhipaḥ paryāptā hi vayaṃ tena saha yodhayituṃ parān
english: "Alas, shame! The king does not know that we still live—for together with him we are enough to fight the foe."

sanskrit: te tu tatra ciraṃ kālaṃ vilapya ca mahārathāḥ prādravan rathināṃ śreṣṭhā dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍusutān raṇe
english: Those great warriors, foremost of charioteers, lamented there a long while, then fled away, having seen Pāṇḍu's sons upon the field.

sanskrit: te tu māṃ ratham āropya kṛpasya supariṣkṛtam senāniveśam ājagmur hataśeṣās trayo rathāḥ
english: Mounting me on Kṛpa's well-furnished chariot, those three warriors, the survivors of the slaughter, came to the army's encampment.

sanskrit: tatra gulmāḥ paritrastāḥ sūrye cāstam ite sati sarve vicukruśuḥ śrutvā putrāṇāṃ tava saṃkṣayam
english: There the terror-stricken guard-posts, as the sun went down, all cried aloud when they heard of the destruction of your sons.

sanskrit: tato vṛddhā mahārāja yoṣitāṃ rakṣaṇo narāḥ rājadārān upādāya prayayur nagaraṃ prati
english: Then the aged men who guarded the women, great king, taking up the royal consorts, set out toward the city.

sanskrit: tatra vikrośatīnāṃ ca rudatīnāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ prādurāsīn mahāñ śabdaḥ śrutvā tad balasaṃkṣayam
english: There arose on every side a mighty clamor of women shrieking and weeping, when they heard of that destruction of the army.

sanskrit: tatas tā yoṣito rājan krandantyo vai muhur muhuḥ kurarya iva śabdena nādayantyo mahītalam
english: Then those women, O king, wailing again and again, made the earth resound with their cries like ospreys.

sanskrit: ājaghnuḥ karajaiś cāpi pāṇibhiś ca śirāṃsy uta luluvuś ca tadā keśān krośantyas tatra tatra ha
english: They beat their heads with their nails and with their hands, and tore their hair, crying out here and there.

sanskrit: hāhākāravinādinyo vinighnantya urāṃsi ca krośantyas tatra ruruduḥ krandamānā viśāṃ pate
english: Wailing their cries of woe and beating their breasts, they shrieked and wept there, lamenting, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanāmātyāḥ sāśrukaṇṭhā bhṛśāturāḥ rājadārān upādāya prayayur nagaraṃ prati
english: Then Duryodhana's counselors, their throats choked with tears and sorely stricken, taking up the royal women, set out toward the city.

sanskrit: vetrajarjharahastāś ca dvārādhyakṣā viśāṃ pate śayanīyāni śubhrāṇi spardhyāstaraṇavanti ca samādāya yayus tūrṇaṃ nagaraṃ dārarakṣiṇaḥ
english: And the gatekeepers, O lord of peoples, with worn canes in their hands, the guardians of the women, gathered up the gleaming couches with their costly coverlets and went swiftly toward the city.

sanskrit: āsthāyāśvatarīyuktān syandanān apare janāḥ svān svān dārān upādāya prayayur nagaraṃ prati
english: Other men, mounting chariots yoked with she-mules, taking up each his own womenfolk, set out toward the city.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvā yā nāryo bhāskareṇāpi veśmasu dadṛśus tā mahārāja janā yāntīḥ puraṃ prati
english: Those women whom even the sun had never before beheld within their chambers, men now saw, great king, as they went toward the city.

sanskrit: tāḥ striyo bharataśreṣṭha saukumāryasamanvitāḥ prayayur nagaraṃ tūrṇaṃ hatasvajanabāndhavāḥ
english: Those tender, delicate women, O best of the Bhāratas, their own kinsmen and relations slain, hastened toward the city.

sanskrit: ā gopālāvipālebhyo dravanto nagaraṃ prati yayur manuṣyāḥ saṃbhrāntā bhīmasenabhayārditāḥ
english: Down to the very cowherds and shepherds, the people fled in confusion toward the city, tormented by fear of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: api caiṣāṃ bhayaṃ tīvraṃ pārthebhyo 'bhūt sudāruṇam prekṣamāṇās tadānyonyam ādhāvan nagaraṃ prati
english: And a fierce, most dreadful fear of the Pārthas was upon them; gazing at one another, they ran toward the city.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tadā vartamāne vidrave bhṛśadāruṇe yuyutsuḥ śokasaṃmūḍhaḥ prāptakālam acintayat
english: While that most terrible rout was taking place, Yuyutsu, bewildered with grief, pondered what the hour demanded.

sanskrit: jito duryodhanaḥ saṃkhye pāṇḍavair bhīmavikramaiḥ ekādaśacamūbhartā bhrātaraś cāsya sūditāḥ hatāś ca kuravaḥ sarve bhīṣmadroṇapuraḥsarāḥ
english: "Duryodhana, lord of eleven armies, is vanquished in battle by the Pāṇḍavas of fearsome valor; his brothers are slain, and all the Kurus, with Bhīṣma and Droṇa at their head, are dead."

sanskrit: aham eko vimuktas tu bhāgyayogād yadṛcchayā vidrutāni ca sarvāṇi śibirāṇi samantataḥ
english: "I alone have escaped, by the working of fortune and by chance, while all the camps are scattered on every side."

sanskrit: duryodhanasya sacivā ye ke cid avaśeṣitāḥ rājadārān upādāya vyadhāvan nagaraṃ prati
english: "Whatever of Duryodhana's ministers are left, they have taken up the royal women and are running toward the city."

sanskrit: prāptakālam ahaṃ manye praveśaṃ taiḥ sahābhibho yudhiṣṭhiram anujñāpya bhīmasenaṃ tathaiva ca
english: "I think the hour has come for me to enter the city along with them, O lord—once I have taken leave of Yudhiṣṭhira and of Bhīmasena as well."

sanskrit: etam arthaṃ mahābāhur ubhayoḥ sa nyavedayat tasya prīto 'bhavad rājā nityaṃ karuṇaveditā pariṣvajya mahābāhur vaiśyāputraṃ vyasarjayat
english: The mighty-armed one set this matter before the two of them; the king, ever moved by compassion, was pleased with him, and the strong-armed one, embracing the son of the vaiśya woman, gave him leave to go.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa ratham āsthāya drutam aśvān acodayat asaṃbhāvitavāṃś cāpi rājadārān puraṃ prati
english: Then, mounting his chariot, he swiftly urged on his horses, and, overtaking the royal women unlooked-for, set off toward the city.

sanskrit: taiś caiva sahitaḥ kṣipram astaṃ gacchati bhāskare praviṣṭo hāstinapuraṃ bāṣpakaṇṭho 'śrulocanaḥ
english: Together with them he swiftly entered Hāstinapura as the sun was setting, his throat choked with tears and his eyes streaming.

sanskrit: apaśyata mahāprājñaṃ viduraṃ sāśrulocanam rājñaḥ samīpān niṣkrāntaṃ śokopahatacetasam
english: He saw the deeply wise Vidura, his eyes too wet with tears, coming out from the king's presence, his mind stricken with grief.

sanskrit: tam abravīt satyadhṛtiḥ praṇataṃ tv agrataḥ sthitam asmin kurukṣaye vṛtte diṣṭyā tvaṃ putra jīvasi
english: To him, who stood bowing before him, the steadfast-in-truth one said: "Now that this destruction of the Kurus has come to pass, by good fortune, my son, you are alive."

sanskrit: vinā rājñaḥ praveśād vai kim asi tvam ihāgataḥ etan me kāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ vistareṇa nivedaya
english: "Yet without the king's own entry, how is it that you have come here? Tell me the whole reason of this in full."

sanskrit: yuyutsur uvāca nihate śakunau tāta sajñātisutabāndhave hataśeṣaparīvāro rājā duryodhanas tataḥ svakaṃ sa hayam utsṛjya prāṅmukhaḥ prādravad bhayāt
english: Yuyutsu said: "When Śakuni was slain, dear sir, with his kinsmen, sons, and relations, then King Duryodhana, with but the remnant of his retinue left, abandoned his own horse and, turning eastward, fled in fear."

sanskrit: apakrānte tu nṛpatau skandhāvāraniveśanāt bhayavyākulitaṃ sarvaṃ prādravan nagaraṃ prati
english: "When the king had withdrawn from the encampment of the host, all the people, distraught with fear, fled toward the city."

sanskrit: tato rājñaḥ kalatrāṇi bhrātṝṇāṃ cāsya sarvaśaḥ vāhaneṣu samāropya stryadhyakṣāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: "Then the keepers of the women, mounting upon the carriages the consorts of the king and of all his brothers, fled in fear."

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ samanujñāpya rājānaṃ sahakeśavam praviṣṭo hāstinapuraṃ rakṣaṃl lokād dhi vācyatām
english: "Then I, having taken leave of the king together with Keśava, entered Hāstinapura, to guard against the world's reproach."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ vaiśyāputreṇa bhāṣitam prāptakālam iti jñātvā viduraḥ sarvadharmavit apūjayad ameyātmā yuyutsuṃ vākyakovidam
english: Hearing these words spoken by the son of the vaiśya woman, and knowing them timely, Vidura, knower of all that is right, of immeasurable soul, honored the eloquent Yuyutsu.

sanskrit: prāptakālam idaṃ sarvaṃ bhavato bharatakṣaye adya tvam iha viśrāntaḥ śvo 'bhigantā yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "All this of yours is timely amid the ruin of the Bhāratas; today rest here, and tomorrow you shall go to Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ viduraḥ sarvadharmavit yuyutsuṃ samanujñāpya praviveśa nṛpakṣayam yuyutsur api tāṃ rātriṃ svagṛhe nyavasat tadā
english: Having spoken these words, Vidura, knower of all that is right, dismissed Yuyutsu and entered the king's dwelling; and Yuyutsu too passed that night in his own house.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca hateṣu sarvasainyeṣu pāṇḍuputrai raṇājire mama sainyāvaśiṣṭās te kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When all my armies had been slain by Pāṇḍu's sons on the field of battle, what did those survivors of my host do, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā kṛpaś caiva droṇaputraś ca vīryavān duryodhanaś ca mandātmā rājā kim akarot tadā
english: Kṛtavarman and Kṛpa, and the valiant son of Droṇa—and King Duryodhana of feeble mind—what did he do then?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃprādravatsu dāreṣu kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahātmanām vidrute śibire śūnye bhṛśodvignās trayo rathāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the women of the great-souled kṣatriyas had fled away and the camp lay empty and abandoned, the three warriors, deeply distraught,

sanskrit: niśamya pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ tadā vijayināṃ svanam vidrutaṃ śibiraṃ dṛṣṭvā sāyāhne rājagṛddhinaḥ sthānaṃ nārocayaṃs tatra tatas te hradam abhyayuḥ
english: hearing the shouts of the victorious sons of Pāṇḍu and seeing the camp deserted at evening, longing for their king, found that place no longer to their liking, and so they went toward the lake.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi dharmātmā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito raṇe hṛṣṭaḥ paryapatad rājan duryodhanavadhepsayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira too, the righteous-souled, together with his brothers, ranged exultant over the field, O king, eager to slay Duryodhana.

sanskrit: mārgamāṇās tu saṃkruddhās tava putraṃ jayaiṣiṇaḥ yatnato 'nveṣamāṇās tu naivāpaśyañ janādhipam
english: Enraged and bent on victory, they searched for your son, seeking him out with all their effort, yet nowhere did they see the lord of men.

sanskrit: sa hi tīvreṇa vegena gadāpāṇir apākramat taṃ hradaṃ prāviśac cāpi viṣṭabhyāpaḥ svamāyayā
english: For he, mace in hand, had withdrawn with swift speed and had entered that lake, holding back its waters by his own magic.

sanskrit: yadā tu pāṇḍavāḥ sarve supariśrāntavāhanāḥ tataḥ svaśibiraṃ prāpya vyatiṣṭhan sahasainikāḥ
english: When at last all the Pāṇḍavas found their teams quite spent, they returned to their own camp and halted there with their soldiers.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛpaś ca drauṇiś ca kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ saṃniviṣṭeṣu pārtheṣu prayātās taṃ hradaṃ śanaiḥ
english: Then Kṛpa and Droṇa's son and Kṛtavarman the Sātvata, while the Pārthas were encamped, set out slowly toward that lake.

sanskrit: te taṃ hradaṃ samāsādya yatra śete janādhipaḥ abhyabhāṣanta durdharṣaṃ rājānaṃ suptam ambhasi
english: Reaching the lake where the lord of men lay, they addressed the unassailable king as he slept within the waters.

sanskrit: rājann uttiṣṭha yudhyasva sahāsmābhir yudhiṣṭhiram jitvā vā pṛthivīṃ bhuṅkṣva hato vā svargam āpnuhi
english: "Rise, O king, and fight beside us! Conquer Yudhiṣṭhira and enjoy the earth, or, slain, attain to heaven."

sanskrit: teṣām api balaṃ sarvaṃ hataṃ duryodhana tvayā pratirabdhāś ca bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ye śiṣṭās tatra sainikāḥ
english: "Their whole force too, Duryodhana, has been struck down by you, and most of those soldiers who remain there are sorely beset."
